title: Multitenant Spotlight Auditor and Remediation Playbook
author: Jordan Kim
body:
Summary
-------
This document describes the Multitenant Spotlight Auditor (MSA): an operator-facing toolkit and service for detecting, scoring, and remediating tenant-level unfairness and negative externalities in our inference platform. MSA centralizes signals from schedulers, KV/prefix cache, token-cost attribution, and tail-latency traces to produce a ranked list of tenants and workloads needing operator attention or automated mitigation.

Goals
-----
- Detect tenant behaviors that cause disproportionate resource impact (latency spikes, cache thrashing, excessive batching stalls, token leakage).
- Provide actionable, auditable comparisons and a repeatable remediation runbook.
- Offer safe automated mitigations with human-in-the-loop escalation.
- Make fairness and cost-impact visible to platform ops and product stakeholders via dashboards and alerts.

Out of scope
--------
- Billing disputes and adjustments (handled by Finance).
- Tenant-facing rate-limiting policy text (handled by API gateway).

When to use MSA
----------------
- After an unexplained regional latency degradation where tenant mix changed.
- When we observe token-cost variance not explained by workload shape.
- As part of capacity planning experiments to validate fairness models.

Architecture (high level)
------------------------
MSA has three main components:
1) Ingest: scheduled jobs and streaming collectors that join traces, cost-attribution, scheduler events, and prefix-KV cache telemetry.
2) Scoring Engine: batch + streaming jobs compute per-tenant impact scores (latency externality, cache churn index, token-leak factor).
3) Operator UI & Automation: a dashboard with ranked incidents, recommended remediations, and automation routines (soft-throttle, tenant-priority-reshuffle, canary requeue).

Diagram (text):
- Traces & Spans -> collector
- Token-cost-attribution -> collector
- Scheduler events (placement/migrations) -> collector
- Collectors -> enrichment layer (join on request_id / prefix_key) -> scoring engine -> DB (audit log)
- Operator UI reads DB and triggers playbook actions via platform APIs

Data model and key signals
--------------------------
- tenant_id (string)
- window_start, window_end (ISO datetime)
- requests_per_minute (numeric)
- p99_latency_ms (numeric)
- mean_queue_depth (numeric)
- cache_prefix_evictions (numeric)
- kv_cache_hit_rate (0..1)
- token_burn_adjusted (numeric) -- tokens charged after prefix caching adjustments
- externality_score (0..100) -- composite computed by scoring engine

Scoring heuristics (summary)
--------------------------
- latency_externality = max(0, p99 - baseline_p99) * weight_latency
- cache_churn_index = normalized(cache_prefix_evictions) * weight_cache
- token_leak_factor = log(1 + token_burn_adjusted / tenant_avg) * weight_token
- externality_score = scaled_sum(latency_externality, cache_churn_index, token_leak_factor)

Baselines and normalization are computed per-region and per-hardware-class to avoid false positives from heterogenous fleets.

SLIs / Alerting rules (recommended)
----------------------------------
- Alert: tenant-spotlight-high-externality
  - Trigger: externality_score >= 75 for 15m AND tenant not in "trusted-tier" list
  - Severity: P2
  - Runbook: follow MSA triage runbook below
- Alert: repeated-cache-thrashing
  - Trigger: cache_prefix_evictions > 10k in 5m AND kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.35
  - Severity: P3

Dashboard wireframe (recommended panels)
---------------------------------------
- Live ranked table: tenant, region, externality_score, p99, token_burn_adjusted, recommended_action
- Time series: top-10 tenants p99 vs region baseline
- Heatmap: cache_evictions per prefix_key across nodes
- Cost lens: token_burn attribution stacked by tenant and model

Runbook: Triage & Remediation (operator steps)
----------------------------------------------
1) Acknowledge alert and open MSA entry for the tenant.
2) Inspect live ranked table and click into tenant timeline. Gather: p99, p50, queue depth, cache eviction trend, model version served.
3) Check recent placement changes in scheduler events for collocated noisy tenants.
4) If cache_churn_index high:
   a) Temporarily pin tenant to dedicated prefix cache shard if available.
   b) For immediate relief, apply soft-ttl increase to small prefixes using API:

   CLI example:
   ```
   rcd platform cache update-ttl --prefix tenant-abc --ttl 120s --reason "MSA mitigation: reduce evictions"
   ```

5) If token_leak_factor high:
   a) Run prompt-set audit to detect patterns causing poor caching (see Appendix Query A).
   b) Recommend model quantization or batching tweak; notify solutions engineering.

6) If latency_externality dominant and no configuration fix found:
   a) Apply soft-throttle on throughput for offending tenant (10-20% reduction) via tenant priority weight:

   CLI example:
   ```
   rcd scheduler set-priority --tenant tenant-abc --weight 0.8 --duration 30m --reason "MSA temporary fairness throttle"
   ```

7) After mitigation, monitor externality_score for 2 windows (each window = 15m). If score does not reduce by 50%, escalate to Platform Escalation channel and follow emergency-model-swap runbook.

Safety & guardrails for automation
----------------------------------
- Automation actions must be approved by one on-call operator except for low-impact actions (ttl tweak <= 120s, soft-priority <= 10%) that can run automatically.
- No automated action may change tenant billing or customer-visible SLA text.
- All automated actions must create an audit record with: actor, reason, pre- and post-metrics snapshot.
- Rollback hooks: each automated change must declare a rollback window (default 60m) and auto-revert if externality_score worsens.

Experimentation and rollout plan
--------------------------------
1) Canary phase (2 weeks): deploy MSA scoring engine in passive mode for 10% of regions. No automation enabled, alerting read-only.
2) Operator trial (4 weeks): enable manual-action buttons, collect operator feedback, tune weights.
3) Controlled automation (6 weeks): enable low-impact automated actions with 1-operator approval gating.
4) Full rollout: automation policy enabled with standard guardrails and monthly audit.

Metrics to track during rollout
- False-positive rate of top-20 flagged tenants (target < 10%)
- Operator time-to-remediation (target < 30 minutes after acknowledging)
- Automation rollback rate (target < 5%)

Ownership, dependencies, and roadmap items
-----------------------------------------
- Primary owner: eng-platform/tenant-observability squad (oncall: @tenant-observability)
- Dependencies:
  - Token cost attribution service (engineering/infra)
  - KV/prefix cache telemetry (eng-serving-runtime)
  - Scheduler events stream (eng-platform/scheduler)
- Next roadmap items: integrate MSA with Optimize recommendations (Q3 2026), expose tenant-level notice to support (Q4 2026).

Operator playbook templates (quick references)
---------------------------------------------
- Template A: Cache evictions mitigation (one-liner)
  - When: cache_prefix_evictions spike > 5x baseline and kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.4
  - Action: update-ttl + pin-prefix-shard + notify product owner
- Template B: Latency externality mitigation (one-liner)
  - When: p99 > baseline + 200ms and queue_depth > 3
  - Action: reduce tenant weight by 10% for 30m; monitor

Appendix: Example queries and alerts
-----------------------------------
- SQL: Top tenants by externality (example)
  ```sql
  SELECT tenant_id,
         SUM(externality_score) AS score,
         MAX(p99_latency_ms) AS p99
  FROM msa.tenant_window
  WHERE window_start >= now() - interval '1 hour'
  GROUP BY tenant_id
  ORDER BY score DESC
  LIMIT 50;
  ```
- Alert rule (PromQL example)
  ```promql
  msa_externality_score{region="us-east-1"} > 75
  ```

Retrospective notes (pilot run 2026-03)
---------------------------------------
- What went well:
  - Early detection reduced mean p99 across impacted regions by ~18% in pilot.
  - Operators found the ranked view accelerated root-cause discovery.
- What to improve:
  - Initial scoring overemphasized short-lived spikes; added smoothing window.
  - Need clearer tenant metadata (product owner, SLA tier) in the UI.

FAQ and related references
-------------------------
- Why not throttle automatically by default? -> We prioritize human-in-loop to avoid breaking customer SLAs.
- How are weights tuned? -> We run offline sensitivity tests with synthetic workloads and validate against historical incidents.
- Related pages: tenant-isolation-economics-playbook-2026, runtime-health-contracts-and-self-heal-orchestration-2026.

Contact and escalation
----------------------
- Primary contacts: eng-platform/tenant-observability squad (oncall), runtime-telemetry team.
- For security-sensitive incidents, follow security-and-compliance/incident-response-security procedures.
